The config migration was small. Preserving the package contract was the interesting part.
Hoi hoi! 👋
I'm @nyaomaru, a frontend engineer who enjoyed looking for fungus this season. 😸🍄
Recently, I migrated its build setup from tsup to tsdown.
At first, I expected this to be a very small task.
Just remove tsup.
tsdown.
And honestly...
The config migration was small.
But there was one interesting problem.
The first tsdown build succeeded while silently changing files that were already part of the package's public contract.
So this article isn't really an introduction to tsdown.
Instead, I want to show what happened when I migrated a real published TypeScript library from tsup to tsdown, what actually changed, and how I verified that consumers would still receive the same package.

No new model. No training. Four sentences of prompt.
ARC-AGI-3 is the cruel exam of the AI world. It hands an agent an unfamiliar video game — grid-world puzzles, checkers variants, web games — and demands it learn the rules from scratch, by playing. No tutorial. The standard way to play it: pipe the game state to the model as a 64×64 numeric text grid, ask what to do next, and count the moves.
On October 1, Qiushi Han, Keya Hu, Linlu Qiu, Cathy Wu, and Kaiming He at MIT CSAIL posted a …
articles.title: The Model Wasn't Stupid. It Was Blind: How a Four-Sentence Prompt Took Claude to a Perfect 100 on ARC-AGI-3

articles.author: Mindinu Ariyawansha
articles.description:
With the rise of autonomous AI agents and code-interpreting LLM features, Node.js backends are increasingly required to execute code generated on the fly. 
However, running arbitrary user or AI code inside a Node.js process is dangerous. A single malicious or hallucinated script can read environment variables (process.env), spawn OS processes (child_process), freeze the event loop with infinite loops, or crash your entire server by exhausting heap memory.
In this post, we’ll analyze the three primary methods for executing isolated code in Node.js, why built-in modules fail at security, and how to implement true V8 heap sandboxing.
vm Module: Great for Context, Terrible for Security


Node.js ships with a built-in vm module that allows compiling and running code within a synthetic context.
…
articles.title: Safely Running AI-Generated Code in Node.js: `vm` vs `worker_threads` vs V8 Isolates

articles.description:
You can clear pip's cache on Windows with py -m pip cache purge after checking its location and size. This removes cached downloads and wheels, not packages already installed in your Python environments. If you only need to remove a particular cached wheel, use a targeted removal instead of purging everything.
Open Start > Command Prompt under your normal development account. These steps assume Python and pip are installed and the py command is available. Run:
py -m pip --version
py -m pip cache dir
py -m pip cache info

Keep the output so you know which installation and cache you inspected. The directory command reports the configured cache; the information command reports its contents and size. They help you decide whether cache cleanup is relevant before any deletion.
The usual Windows …

articles.description:
We asked Claude Sonnet and Haiku to humanize one text in five languages. Without rules, all ten answers lost the word usually, and some invented facts.
Not reliably, if all you send is the request. Claude Sonnet and Claude Haiku each received one short piece of AI-sounding text in five languages, with nothing more than the line "Humanize this text." In all ten of them the word "usually" was gone, so a meeting the company usually holds once a year turned into one it always holds. Sonnet's answers stated facts the input never gave, and Haiku's added motives nobody had claimed and came back in English for three of the four non-English texts. Once the same models had our rules for this task loaded as a skill, all ten answers kept that qualifier, stayed in the original language and returned nothing but the rewrite, though both models still cut…
Read the full report on AISkills402: https://aiskills402.com/blog/llm-humanize-drops-usually
articles.title: Humanizing AI text with an LLM: what goes missing

You ask Claude Code to change one function, and it greps for the name, opens a 900-line file, reads half of it, opens three more files, and your context window is gone before the first edit. Then the rename it does is a dozen fragile find-and-replace edits that still miss a call site.

With uv installed, these three commands do the whole setup:
uv tool install -p 3.13 serena-agent
serena init
s…

articles.author: Arkendu Kundu
articles.description:
friendstudy ai — an open-source ai study companion 📚🤖


what if studying had a personal ai companion that could help you plan, learn, practice, and stay consistent?
that's the idea behind friendstudy ai.
i built friendstudy ai as an open-source ai-powered study companion for students who struggle with planning their studies, understanding difficult topics, and staying consistent.
💬 ask ai questions and get explanations
📅 generate personalized study plans
🧠 create practice quizzes
🎯 manage daily study goals
📊 track study progress
🔥 maintain study streaks
📚 make studying more structured and consistent
instead of relying entirely on proprietary ai APIs, friendstudy ai uses qwen 2.5 3b through ollama.
the goal was to experiment with open-weight ai and understand what it takes to build a complete ai-powered application around an open model.
frontend: react + javascript

backend: python + fastapi

ai: qwen 2.5 3b + ollama

deployment: vercel + render
🌐 live demo:

https://friendstudy-ai-hf26.vercel.app/
💻 github:

https://github.com/arkendukundu-dev/friendstudy-ai-hf26
building this project taught me how different pieces of an ai application come together — from frontend and backend development to model integration, api communication, debugging, and deployment.
the biggest takeaway for me was:
building with ai isn't just about using a model. it's about building a useful product around it.
i built friendstudy ai for the launch weekend dev challenge and i'm excited to keep improving it with better personalization, smarter study plans, stronger quizzes, and more open-source models.
if you're a student, give it a try and let me know what you think! 🚀
articles.title: FriendStudy AI — Your Open-Source AI Study Companion
